title: Participle & absolute constructions
note: present participle as condensed adverbial (+ the same-subject rule and Not + -ing) · perfect participle Having + PP and the passive Having been + PP · past participle clauses and reduced relatives, active -ing vs passive -ed · absolute constructions, with + noun + participle/adjective, and the fixed phrases (that said, weather permitting, all things considered) · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 12)

cards.title: Cutting a clause down to a participle
cards.title_cz: Jak z vedlejší věty udělat participium
cards.body: A participle clause says the same thing as a full subordinate clause with fewer words: the subject and the finite verb go, and a participle carries what is left. English writing leans on this heavily; Czech reaches for a full clause far more often, which is why these feel compressed at first.
cards.body_cz: Participiální vazba řekne totéž co celá vedlejší věta, jen s menším počtem slov: podmět a určité sloveso zmizí a zbytek unese participium. Psaná angličtina se o tuhle vazbu opírá velmi silně; čeština sáhne mnohem častěji po celé větě, a proto tyhle tvary zpočátku působí stlačeně.

table.caption: the same sentence, twice
rows: While I was walking home, I met an old friend.
Walking home, I met an old friend.
After he had finished the report, he went home.
Having finished the report, he went home.
The letters which were sent last week…
The letters sent last week…
Because the weather was fine, we walked.
The weather being fine, we walked.

cards.title: Which participle, and when
cards.body: Three forms, three jobs. The -ing form is active and happens at the same time. Having + past participle is active and happens first. The bare past participle is passive — the noun receives the action.
cards.body_cz: Tři tvary, tři úkoly. Tvar s -ing je činný a děje se současně. Having + příčestí minulé je činné a děje se dřív. Holé příčestí minulé je trpné — podstatné jméno děj přijímá.

table.caption: choose by voice and by order
rows: -ing
active
same time
Feeling tired, he went to bed early.
Having + PP
active
earlier
Having missed the last bus, they walked home.
past participle
passive
same time or earlier
Written in 1920, the novel still sells.
Having been + PP
passive
earlier
Having been told the news, she sat down.

points: The negative goes in front of the whole thing: Not knowing the answer, …
Not *Knowing not the answer* and not *Don't knowing*.

cards.title: The rule that decides whether it is right
cards.body: A participle clause has no subject of its own, so English reads its subject off the main clause. If the two do not match, the participle dangles and the sentence says something absurd. This is the single most common C1 error with this structure — and the only reliable fix is to check who is doing what.
cards.body_cz: Participiální vazba nemá vlastní podmět, a tak si ho angličtina přečte z věty hlavní. Pokud si oba neodpovídají, participium „visí“ a věta říká nesmysl. Je to nejčastější chyba na úrovni C1 u téhle vazby — a jediná spolehlivá oprava je zkontrolovat, kdo co dělá.

table.caption: who is doing the -ing?
rows: Walking home, the rain started.
the rain was not walking
Walking home, I got wet.
Having finished the report, the office was empty.
the office did not finish it
Having finished the report, he found the office empty.
Being a doctor, the question was easy for her.
the question is not a doctor
Being a doctor, she found the question easy.

cards.title: Cutting a relative clause
cards.body: A relative clause can lose its pronoun and its form of be, but only when the pronoun is the subject of that clause. Active becomes -ing, passive becomes the bare past participle.
cards.body_cz: Vztažná věta může přijít o zájmeno i o tvar slovesa be, ale jen tehdy, je-li zájmeno podmětem té věty. Z činného tvaru se stane -ing, z trpného holé příčestí minulé.

table.caption: active -ing, passive -ed
rows: the train which is leaving from platform three
the train leaving from platform three
students who live far from the school
students living far from the school
the man who was arrested last night
the man arrested last night
the questions which were asked at the meeting
the questions asked at the meeting

points: Object relatives cannot be reduced this way: the book that I read stays as it is.
Once opened, … and Once finished, … are the same reduction after a conjunction.

cards.title: Absolutes: the clause that keeps its own subject
cards.title_cz: Absolutní vazba: ta, která si podmět ponechá
cards.body: An absolute construction keeps a subject of its own, so it is free to talk about something other than the main clause — the one participle structure that cannot dangle. Bare noun + participle is formal and literary; with + noun is the version you will hear in ordinary speech.
cards.body_cz: Absolutní vazba si ponechává vlastní podmět, a může tedy mluvit o něčem jiném než věta hlavní — je to jediná participiální vazba, která nemůže „viset“. Holé podstatné jméno + participium je formální a knižní; varianta s with je ta, kterou uslyšíte v běžné řeči.

table.caption: the everyday one is with
rows: noun + -ing
The weather being fine, we walked into town.
noun + past participle
Her work finished, she left the office.
noun + adjective / adverb
The meeting over, everybody went home.
with + noun + -ing
With prices going up, many families are worried.
with + noun + adjective
With the window open, the room was very cold.

points: There being no questions, … keeps the dummy there as its subject.
Fixed phrases to learn whole: that said · weather permitting · all things considered.
These are the sentences where a Czech speaker most often reaches for a full clause — and is not wrong to, only less concise.

table.caption: check
rows: Walking home, the rain started.
Walking home, I got wet.
Knowing not the answer, she stayed quiet.
Not knowing the answer, she stayed quiet.
Having finish the report, he went home.
Having finished the report, he went home.
Being told the news yesterday, she sat down.
Having been told the news, she sat down.
The letters which sent last week have not arrived.
The letters sent last week have not arrived.
Writing in 1920, the novel still sells well.
Written in 1920, the novel still sells well.
All things considering, the evening went well.
All things considered, the evening went well.
The weather was fine, we walked into town.
The weather being fine, we walked into town.

items.gap: ____ home, I met an old friend.

items.explanation: A present participle clause condenses an adverbial clause of time, reason or accompanying action: drop the subject and the finite verb and use the -ing form. It is only correct when both halves share the same subject — otherwise the participle dangles. The negative goes in front: Not knowing the answer, …
items.explanation_cz: Participiální vazba s -ing zhustí vedlejší větu časovou, příčinnou nebo větu vyjadřující doprovodný děj: vypustí se podmět i určité sloveso a zůstane tvar s -ing. Je správná jen tehdy, mají-li obě části stejný podmět — jinak participium „visí“ ve vzduchu. Zápor stojí vpředu: Not knowing the answer, …

items.explanation: Having + past participle marks the first action as finished before the second begins; use it instead of the plain -ing form when the two events are in sequence rather than simultaneous. The passive is Having been + past participle. The same-subject rule still applies.
items.explanation_cz: Having + příčestí minulé říká, že první děj skončil dřív, než začal druhý; použije se místo prostého tvaru s -ing tehdy, jdou-li děje po sobě, a ne současně. Trpný rod zní Having been + příčestí minulé. Pravidlo o stejném podmětu platí i tady.

items.explanation: An absolute construction carries its own subject, so it does not have to match the subject of the main clause — this is the one participle structure that cannot dangle. The bare form is noun + participle (The weather being fine, …); with + noun + participle, adjective or prepositional phrase is the everyday version. A handful are fixed phrases: that said, weather permitting, all things considered.
items.explanation_cz: Absolutní vazba má vlastní podmět, takže se nemusí shodovat s podmětem věty hlavní — je to jediná participiální vazba, která nemůže „viset“. Holý tvar je podstatné jméno + participium (The weather being fine, …); běžnější varianta je with + podstatné jméno + participium, přídavné jméno nebo předložková vazba. Několik spojení je ustálených: that said, weather permitting, all things considered.

Holý tvar je podstatné jméno + participium (The weather being fine, …); běžnější varianta je with + podstatné jméno + participium, přídavné jméno nebo předložková vazba. Několik spojení je ustálených: that said, weather permitting, all things considered.

accepts: With the children asleep, the house was silent.
